hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

informal_arrangement.description: Whether the claimant is looking after someone else's child through an informal arrangement.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. I can see you're asking about Child Benefit for Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you in the UK.

To assess your eligibility properly, I need to clarify one important detail:

You mentioned that you're not Alex's parent or official carer and that you look after Alex through an informal arrangement. Can you tell me:

1. **Are you contributing financially to Alex's upkeep?** (This would include things like food, clothes, pocket money, or paying for their accommodation)

2. **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's parent or another relative)

This information is important because the rules state that you may be able to get Child Benefit if you've got an informal arrangement to look after a friend or relative's child, but only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child. Also, you'll usually be responsible for a child if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them.

Please let me know these details so I can give you an accurate assessment.

## **Good News! You Are Eligible for Child Benefit**

Based on your circumstances, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why you're eligible:

✓ **Alex is 8 years old** (under 16)  
✓ **Alex lives with you** in the UK  
✓ **You are responsible for Alex** through an informal arrangement  
✓ **No one else has priority** to claim for Alex  
✓ Alex meets all the other requirements (not in care, not working 24+ hours, etc.)

### What you need to know:

- Even though you're looking after Alex through an informal arrangement (rather than being their parent or official carer), you can still claim Child Benefit as long as you're responsible for them - which you are, since Alex lives with you.

- **Important:** Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, so make sure no one else (like Alex's parents) is currently claiming for them. If they are, you'll need to agree who should claim.

### Next steps:

You can [make a claim for Child Benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim) online or by post.

If you have any questions about making your claim, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for assistance.
